payload.prompt: What can generative AI produce?

options.rationale: Generative AI creates new content that can resemble human-created work. Poetry, prose, and code are examples.
Stored documents are existing material, not newly created output. Generative AI generates a new response.
options.better_fit: Retrieval fits locating source documents.

feedback.intrinsic: This would return existing material.
feedback.instructional: Generation creates new content; retrieval finds existing information.

options.rationale: Tools perform actions in external systems. Content creation is generative AI's defining capability.
options.better_fit: An AI agent can use tools to update a calendar.

feedback.intrinsic: A drafting task would be treated as an action.
feedback.instructional: Separate generated content from agent actions.

options.rationale: Token identifiers label language units. They are not prose, poetry, or code.
options.better_fit: Token IDs identify units in a vocabulary.

feedback.intrinsic: You would focus on labels instead of content.
feedback.instructional: Tokens support processing; generative AI produces content.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Generative AI creates original human-like content.

payload.prompt: Which are examples of content generative AI can produce? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Poetry is original human-like content. Generative AI can create it.
Prose is written content. Generative AI can produce it.
Computer code can be generated as new content. It is a common generative-AI output.
A calendar tool performs an external action. It is not content generated by a model.
options.better_fit: A calendar tool fits an agent that changes events.

feedback.intrinsic: This mixes a tool with generated output.
feedback.instructional: Choose created writing or code, not a system action.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Poetry, prose, and code are generative-AI outputs.

payload.prompt: True or false?
payload.statement: Generative AI can only return stored training documents and cannot create new content.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Generative AI produces new, human-like content rather than only returning stored documents.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This would confuse generation with document retrieval.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Generative AI creates original content such as prose, poetry, and code.

payload.prompt: The technology category that creates new content such as poetry, prose, and code is _____.

parts.text: The technology category that creates new content such as poetry, prose, and code is

payload.explanation: Generative AI is the term for AI that creates original human-like content.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The answer would name task automation rather than content creation.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use generative AI for systems that create new prose, poetry, code, and similar content.

payload.prompt: What can both LLMs and SLMs do? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Both model sizes can reason over language input. This supports interpreting a request.
Both LLMs and SLMs can generate meaningful, relevant responses. Learned relationships support this capability.
Both types use learned relationships among words and phrases. Those relationships support reasoning and generation.
A language model processes and generates language. Sending email is an external action requiring a tool-enabled agent.
options.better_fit: An agent with an email tool can send an approved message.

feedback.intrinsic: Drafting an email would be confused with sending it.
feedback.instructional: Language reasoning differs from taking an external action.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Both types use learned relationships to understand input and generate responses.

payload.prompt: What is an SLM?

options.text: A more compact relation of an LLM
options.rationale: SLM means small language model. It is a more compact relation of a large language model.

options.text: A prompt that sets model behavior
options.rationale: A system prompt guides behavior and constraints. It is not a language-model type.
options.better_fit: A system prompt fits standing instructions for an assistant.

feedback.intrinsic: An instruction would be labeled as a model.
feedback.instructional: An SLM is a compact model; a system prompt is guidance.

options.rationale: Search locates information in documents. An SLM processes and generates language.
options.better_fit: A search tool fits locating relevant documents.

feedback.intrinsic: You would seek a search function instead of a model.
feedback.instructional: Search retrieves information; an SLM processes language.

options.rationale: Training data is material used for learning. An SLM is the resulting language model.
options.better_fit: Training data fits text used to learn patterns.

feedback.intrinsic: Learning material would be confused with the model.
feedback.instructional: Keep training data separate from the language model.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. An SLM is a more compact relation of an LLM.

payload.prompt: Decide whether this statement is true or false.
payload.statement: Both LLMs and SLMs can use learned language relationships to generate meaningful, relevant responses.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Both types can use learned relationships to reason over language and generate responses.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Choosing false would reserve response generation for only one model size.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: LLMs and SLMs both use learned language relationships for natural-language responses.

payload.prompt: Put the pieces in order to state what an LLM captures.
payload.explanation: An LLM captures linguistic and semantic relationships among words and phrases.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The statement would not clearly identify what an LLM captures.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Begin with the LLM, then state that it captures relationships among words and phrases.

payload.prompt: The abbreviation for a more compact relation of a large language model is _____.

parts.text: The abbreviation for a more compact relation of a large language model is

payload.explanation: SLM stands for small language model, the compact relation of an LLM.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The answer would name a different model or broader concept.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The S in SLM identifies the small language model.

payload.prompt: An expenses assistant must interpret an employee's question and write a relevant reply. Which language-model capabilities should the developer rely on? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: The employee's question must be interpreted as language input. Reasoning supports an appropriate reply.

options.text: Use relationships between words and phrases
options.rationale: Learned relationships help the model interpret wording and meaning. They support relevant output.
The intended result is a written response addressing the question. Generating a meaningful response is a language-model capability.

options.text: Assign every token a new ID
options.rationale: Assigning IDs concerns vocabulary representation, not answering this question. The assistant should use existing learned relationships.
options.better_fit: Token IDs fit identifying tokenized vocabulary units.

feedback.intrinsic: The developer would relabel units instead of answering.
feedback.instructional: Use learned language relationships to interpret the request and generate a reply.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The model must understand language and generate a relevant response.

payload.prompt: What do semantic relationships concern?

options.rationale: Semantic relationships concern meanings and concepts associated with words and phrases. They describe what language refers to.
Sentence structure concerns linguistic relationships. Semantic relationships concern meaning.
options.better_fit: Linguistic relationships fit how words form meaningful sentences.

feedback.intrinsic: You would judge meaning by grammar alone.
feedback.instructional: Linguistic concerns structure; semantic concerns meaning.

options.rationale: Token position indicates order in a sequence. It does not define a word's meaning.
options.better_fit: Positional encoding fits information about token order.

feedback.intrinsic: Location would be mistaken for meaning.
feedback.instructional: Semantic relationships concern meanings and concepts.

options.rationale: Vector values are numeric representation components. They are not the definition of semantic relationships.
options.better_fit: Embedding vectors can represent learned contextual relationships.

feedback.intrinsic: A representation would be named instead of a relationship type.
feedback.instructional: Semantic relationships are relationships of meaning.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Semantic relationships concern meanings and concepts.

payload.prompt: Is the following statement accurate?
payload.statement: Linguistic relationships primarily concern the concepts and meanings associated with words.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Meanings and concepts are semantic relationships; linguistic relationships concern structure.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The two relationship types would be reversed.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use linguistic for structure and semantic for meanings and concepts.

payload.prompt: Relationships that describe how words and phrases form meaningful sentences are _____.

parts.text: Relationships that describe how words and phrases form meaningful sentences are

payload.explanation: Linguistic relationships concern language structure and how words and phrases form meaningful sentences.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The answer would focus on meaning rather than structure.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Choose linguistic for structural relationships in language.

payload.prompt: Arrange the parts to form a correct statement.
payload.explanation: Linguistic relationships concern the structural side of language, including sentence formation.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The statement would not identify the structural relationship type.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Place the relationship type first, then state what it concerns.

payload.prompt: A developer needs a model to recognize that "cats chase mice" conveys an idea about animals and behavior. Which relationship should the developer use?

options.rationale: The connection among cats, mice, and chasing concerns concepts and meanings. That makes it semantic.
Linguistic relationships concern sentence structure. The decision depends on animal-behavior meaning.
options.better_fit: A linguistic relationship fits deciding grammatical word order.

feedback.intrinsic: The model would focus on grammar while missing the idea.
feedback.instructional: Use semantic relationships when meaning and concepts decide the answer.

options.rationale: A token ID labels a language unit. It does not represent the animal-behavior concept.
options.better_fit: A token ID fits referring to a vocabulary item.

feedback.intrinsic: A numeric label would be treated as conceptual knowledge.
feedback.instructional: Token IDs identify units; semantic relationships capture meaning.

options.rationale: Positional encoding indicates sequence order. It does not supply the underlying concept.
options.better_fit: Positional encoding fits deciding where a token occurs.

feedback.intrinsic: Order information would be mistaken for meaning.
feedback.instructional: The needed clue is meaning, so use a semantic relationship.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The relationship depends on meanings and concepts.

payload.prompt: What helps make "bark" a likely continuation of "I heard a dog ..."? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Heard suggests that a sound may follow. It narrows likely continuations.
Dog is a clue about a likely sound. It supports predicting bark.
Knowledge about dogs provides semantic context. It makes bark plausible.
The model predicts from the available sequence. Later tokens are not known yet.
options.better_fit: Earlier prompt tokens fit next-token context.

feedback.intrinsic: The completion would depend on unseen text.
feedback.instructional: Predict from preceding context such as heard and dog.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Prior words and learned knowledge make bark likely.

payload.prompt: How do LLMs generate a completion?

options.text: By predicting likely tokens in sequence
options.rationale: An LLM predicts likely tokens one after another. Each new token becomes context for the next prediction.
Completions are generated through iterative prediction. Retrieval is different from copying one answer.
options.better_fit: Retrieval fits locating relevant material as context.

feedback.intrinsic: A new request could receive an unchanged stored reply.
feedback.instructional: LLMs generate completions by predicting likely tokens in sequence.

options.rationale: A system prompt sets guidance and constraints. It does not perform token-by-token generation.
options.better_fit: A system prompt fits setting overall assistant instructions.

feedback.intrinsic: Guidance would be mistaken for the writing process.
feedback.instructional: Prompts guide responses; token prediction generates them.

options.rationale: An action tool works outside text generation. An LLM creates text through token prediction.
options.better_fit: An action tool fits an agent completing an external task.

feedback.intrinsic: An external action would be expected instead of text.
feedback.instructional: Separate agent actions from language-model prediction.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. LLMs build completions through sequential token prediction.

payload.prompt: Evaluate this statement.
payload.statement: LLMs can be compared to highly powerful predictive text because they predict likely continuations.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Likely-continuation prediction is the basis of the comparison.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Choosing false would miss the process used to build completions.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: An LLM repeatedly predicts probable next tokens from context.

payload.prompt: Arrange the steps for generating a completion.
payload.explanation: The prompt starts the sequence. A likely token is predicted, added, then supports the next prediction.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The next prediction would lack generated context.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Begin with the prompt, predict one token, add it, then predict again.

payload.prompt: A writing assistant must finish the sentence "The project deadline is ...". Which completions are reasonable choices based on this context? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: A time expression can grammatically and meaningfully follow is. It is plausible for a deadline statement.
Approaching forms a meaningful predicate with the prompt. It is a plausible continuation.
A bicycle does not plausibly describe a deadline. It fails the semantic context.
options.better_fit: A bicycle fits a sentence identifying an object.

feedback.intrinsic: The deadline sentence would become nonsensical.
feedback.instructional: Choose tokens that fit both grammar and meaning.

options.rationale: A token identifier is a label used in a vocabulary. It does not complete this deadline sentence naturally.
options.better_fit: A token identifier fits discussing how a vocabulary represents one token.

feedback.intrinsic: A technical label would replace a meaningful completion.
feedback.instructional: Likely tokens must form a meaningful continuation with the prompt.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Both choices can meaningfully follow the sentence.

payload.prompt: What is a prompt?

options.rationale: A prompt is input given to an LLM for a response. It can be a question, command, or casual comment.
Generated response text is a completion. A prompt is the input that precedes it.
options.better_fit: A completion fits text generated in response to a prompt.

feedback.intrinsic: You would label the reply as the request.
feedback.instructional: A prompt goes in; a completion comes back.

options.rationale: A vocabulary is a collection of available language units. A prompt is one specific input.
options.better_fit: A model vocabulary fits the collection of language units.

feedback.intrinsic: A collection would be mistaken for a request.
feedback.instructional: A prompt is language input supplied to a model.

options.text: A tool used by an agent
options.rationale: An agent tool provides an action or information capability. A prompt is language input to an LLM.
options.better_fit: An agent tool fits searching or sending a message.

feedback.intrinsic: A written request would be confused with a capability.
feedback.instructional: Prompts are inputs; tools are capabilities.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. A prompt is input given to an LLM.

payload.prompt: True or false?
payload.statement: A completion is the question, command, or comment a person gives to an LLM.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. That input is a prompt; a completion is generated output.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The input and output would be reversed.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: A prompt is supplied to the LLM, and a completion is generated in response.

payload.prompt: The text an LLM generates after receiving a prompt is called a _____.

parts.text: The text an LLM generates after receiving a prompt is called a

payload.explanation: A completion is generated response text; a prompt is the input requesting it.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The response would be mislabeled as input.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use completion for text generated by the LLM.

payload.prompt: Reconstruct the statement from the pieces.
payload.explanation: A completion is text generated by an LLM in response to a prompt.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The definition would not clearly identify generated output.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Name the completion first, then state that it is generated text.

payload.prompt: An employee submits the text "Summarize this expense report in three bullets." The assistant must classify that text. What is it?

options.rationale: The employee supplied input requesting a response. Therefore it is a prompt.
A completion is generated after input is received. This employee text is the request, not the output.
options.better_fit: The resulting three-bullet summary would be a completion.

feedback.intrinsic: The request would be mislabeled as its future response.
feedback.instructional: Classify user-supplied input as a prompt.

options.rationale: A system prompt provides standing application guidance. This is a specific employee request.
options.better_fit: A system prompt fits instructions such as "Use a concise professional tone."

feedback.intrinsic: A one-time request would be confused with application rules.
feedback.instructional: System prompts guide overall behavior; this asks for one response.

options.rationale: A predicted token is one unit generated during a completion. This full instruction is input containing multiple tokens.
options.better_fit: A predicted token fits one unit selected while producing the summary.

feedback.intrinsic: A full request would be reduced to one generated unit.
feedback.instructional: The supplied instruction is a prompt, not a predicted token.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The employee's input is a prompt.

payload.prompt: What does training data help a language model do? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Training data provides language material from which vocabulary can be built. It supplies available language units.
Training data exposes the model to language use and patterns. This supports learned relationships.
A large body of training text contains many language units. These can contribute to vocabulary.
The current prompt specifies a requested format. Training data is used earlier for learning.
options.better_fit: A prompt fits asking for bullets or a table.

feedback.intrinsic: The requested format could be ignored as training material.
feedback.instructional: Use prompts for current instructions; training data supports learning.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Training data builds vocabulary and supports pattern learning.

payload.prompt: What is a model vocabulary?

options.text: Language units the model can use
options.rationale: A vocabulary is the collection of language units available to a model. These units are tokens.
Conversation history contains earlier interaction context. A vocabulary is the model's collection of language units.
options.better_fit: Conversation history fits prior prompts and responses used as context.

feedback.intrinsic: A changing conversation would be confused with language units.
feedback.instructional: Vocabulary is a collection of tokens, not chat history.

options.rationale: Agent tools provide actions or information access. A vocabulary contains language units.
options.better_fit: A tool list fits an agent's action capabilities.

feedback.intrinsic: You would look for actions rather than language units.
feedback.instructional: Vocabulary is about language; tools are about capabilities.

options.rationale: A token ID labels one token. A vocabulary is the complete collection of tokens.
options.better_fit: A token ID fits identifying one vocabulary item.

feedback.intrinsic: One label would be mistaken for its collection.
feedback.instructional: Vocabulary is the collection; a token ID identifies one item.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. A vocabulary is the collection of language units a model can use.

payload.prompt: Decide whether this statement is true or false.
payload.statement: Modern LLM vocabularies can contain hundreds of thousands of tokens.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Modern LLM vocabularies can contain hundreds of thousands of tokens.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Choosing false would underestimate the number of available language units.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Modern LLM vocabularies can be very large.

payload.prompt: Put the pieces in the correct order.
payload.explanation: Training data is a large body of text used to learn patterns and build vocabulary.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The definition would not connect the text collection to learning.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start with training data, then describe it as text used to learn patterns.

payload.prompt: A developer is choosing material to build a language model's vocabulary and help it learn language patterns. Which choices are suitable training data? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Training data is a large body of text. A large collection supports vocabulary building and pattern learning.
Modern LLM vocabularies can draw on Internet text. Such text can form part of training data.
Training data can come from Internet and other sources. It must be substantial text used for learning.
A single token ID labels one language unit. It is not the large body of text needed to learn patterns.
options.better_fit: A token ID fits identifying a token after tokenization.

feedback.instructional: Choose substantial text collections as training data; IDs label units within them.
